title: Recover from a mistaken edit
goal: Distinguish undo, discarding unsaved edits and restoring a saved mistake.
challenge: Demonstrate vi undo and discard without changing note.txt, then save a deliberate mistake. Preserve that mistaken file, restore the original bytes and metadata, and prove the original backup remains unchanged.

steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace. Stop if creation or cd fails. Retain its printed path; variables do not survive disk Resume.
steps.expected: A fresh directory inside the guest home; no existing files are changed.

steps.command: printf '%s\n' safe 'retained line' > note.txt; cp -p note.txt original.txt; sha256sum original.txt > original.sha256

steps.explanation: Escape, 1G, 0, cw; type WRONG; Escape; u to undo. Then cw and type UNSAVED; Escape; :q! Enter to discard. Undo is in the current editor; discard does not undo earlier saved files.
Check no change, then deliberately replace safe with broken using 1G, 0, cw; Escape; :wq Enter.

steps.command: diff -u original.txt note.txt; cp -p note.txt saved-mistake.txt; cp -p original.txt note.txt; cmp original.txt note.txt; sha256sum -c original.sha256
steps.explanation: Preserve the mistake before restoration. A saved change needs a retained original, not merely :q!.
steps.expected: Exact rollback and untouched backup; mistake retained.

hints: Which recovery action works after a change has already been saved?
Compare actual output, immediate exit status and resulting files. A syntactically valid command or script can still do the wrong thing.
Keep the original, verify a small intended change, and demonstrate rollback inside this workspace.
review: I retained the stated observations and can explain the outcome.
I checked failure cases and preserved originals; my review is not an application-verified score.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 103.8, 103.3 file recovery reinforcement. Reinforcement is labeled; no full-objective mastery. Completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
